threads.body: Directly accessing `response.response_id` can raise `AttributeError` on supported `google-genai` versions where this field is absent, and in streaming it can also overwrite a previously captured response id with `None` on later chunks. Prefer a guarded, write-once assignment (and coerce to `str`).

replies.body:
Ok your comment made me realize we were parsing the GenerateContentConfig inconsistently all over the place, instead of just doing it in one place, one way and then passing it around..

Ultimately decided to try to use `model_validate` when it's a dict, and return a base empty object when that fails, and pass that around so everything just expects a GenerateContentConfig object..

When I call the real `generate_content` I pass in the original unmodified config (that might have failed to parse, since I don't want to override how the real library deals with a invalid config being passed in..) unless we got a valid config with tools which we wrapped to get the execute tool span..
